about.title: Calabasas Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: When a product fails the way it wasn't supposed to — a car component that gives out on US-101, a household appliance that malfunctions, or protective gear that doesn't hold up on the trails near Mulholland Highway — the consequences can be serious and lasting. Calabasas residents dealing with these injuries often face confusing questions about who's responsible: the manufacturer, the distributor, or the retailer who sold the item. California law generally allows injured people to pursue strict liability claims, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective, not on proving someone was careless. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects you with an independent attorney working on contingency in the Calabasas area. If a product has hurt you or someone you love, holding onto the item itself and getting informed early can make a real difference. Reaching out costs nothing and there's no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: What California's Strict Liability Standard Means for You

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rules, you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury — not that the company was careless. That can simplify what you have to prove.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. An attorney can help sort out who was involved in getting that product to you.

items.title: The Product Itself Matters
items.desc: Design, manufacturing, and warning defects are all recognized categories under California law. Keeping the item — rather than discarding it — helps preserve evidence that may support your claim.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: No. California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, which means the focus is on the product's condition, not the manufacturer's conduct. You typically just need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury.

items.question: I still have the product that hurt me — does that matter?
items.answer: Yes, very much. Preserving the product in its post-incident condition can be important evidence, whether it's a car part involved in a crash on Las Virgenes Road or Calabasas Road, or a household item that malfunctioned. Try not to repair, discard, or alter it before speaking with an attorney.

items.question: What if I bought the product somewhere outside Calabasas?
items.answer: Where you purchased the product usually doesn't prevent you from pursuing a claim if you were injured while using it in Calabasas or elsewhere in Los Angeles County. What matters more is the product itself, how it failed, and the injury it caused. An independent attorney can review the specifics with you at no cost.
